# <Title>

What this governs, and which phase of [WORKFLOW.md](../../WORKFLOW.md) reads it.
One or two sentences on how it differs from the neighbouring standing doc — the
principles/standards and principles/direction pairs are easy to blur.

> A rule here should be able to **reject a design**. If it can't, it is a slogan.
> Prefer one rule with the case that forced it over five that sound agreeable.

## <Rule or area>

The rule, stated so someone who did not write it can apply it.

**Demonstrated by:** where the product already behaves this way, or the incident
that produced the rule.

**Rejects:** the concrete thing this rules out. This line is what makes the rule
citable in a review.

## To write

The questions in this area that have not needed an answer yet. Leaving them as
headings is better than guessing — a rule nobody agreed to still gets cited once
it is written down, and then it is load-bearing by accident.

## Amendments

Standing docs are amended deliberately, in their own commit, never as a side
effect of a feature. The history is most of the value: a principle whose origin
nobody remembers gets ignored.
